title: Linear prefix values from consistency checks
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $w_0,[0m\ldots,w_{n-1}$ be Boolean values, and let a Boolean table assign values to the indices for linear prefixes, quadratic prefixes, and coordinate products. Suppose the table satisfies all of the following checks: the linear prefix at $0$ is false; the quadratic prefix at $0$ is false and at $n$ is true; for each $i<n$, the linear prefix at $i+1$ is the sum in $\mathbb F_2$ of the linear prefix at $i$ and the image of $w_i$; the product entry at $i$ is the Boolean conjunction of the linear prefix at $i$ and $w_i$; and the quadratic prefix at $i+1$ is the sum in $\mathbb F_2$ of the quadratic prefix at $i$ and the image of that product entry. Then for every $k\le n$, the image in $\mathbb F_2$ of the table's linear prefix at $k$ equals the sum of the images of those $w_i$ with $i<k$.
hypotheses_covered: $w$ is a Boolean sequence indexed by $0,\ldots,n-1$
the proof table is Boolean-valued on the specified prefix and product indices
all endpoint and transition checks hold
$k$ is an integer with $0\le k\le n$
